instruction:
Use ESA’s official mission pages to compare Gaia, Euclid and Cheops. For each mission report its launch date, named orbit or destination, the astronomical targets it studies and the main scientific question or measurement described in the mission overview. Order the missions by launch date. Explain which two overviews name the same Lagrange-point destination and which mission instead describes an Earth orbit; retain the wording used by ESA rather than inferring a location from an illustration. Contrast the target populations and scientific purpose so the three missions are not described as interchangeable planet-search telescopes. Cite the three mission pages and record the information shown during the run. Limit the research to the three ESA mission overviews, rather than future release schedules or external mission sites.

Stopping condition: Stop when the three-mission table, launch order, orbit/destination comparison and distinct science purposes are supported by three ESA mission-overview citations.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Report the launch date, named orbit or destination, astronomical targets, and main scientific question or measurement for the Gaia mission based on its ESA mission overview page. Full credit if all four elements are accurately reported, or if the page is unavailable or lacks this information and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if some elements are missing but the page was accessible and contained the information.

Report the launch date, named orbit or destination, astronomical targets, and main scientific question or measurement for the Euclid mission based on its ESA mission overview page. Full credit if all four elements are accurately reported, or if the page is unavailable or lacks this information and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if some elements are missing but the page was accessible and contained the information.

Report the launch date, named orbit or destination, astronomical targets, and main scientific question or measurement for the Cheops mission based on its ESA mission overview page. Full credit if all four elements are accurately reported, or if the page is unavailable or lacks this information and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if some elements are missing but the page was accessible and contained the information.

Present the three missions ordered by their launch dates. Full credit if the missions are ordered correctly according to the dates extracted, or if missing dates due to page unavailability prevent full ordering and the agent notes this. No credit if ordered incorrectly when launch dates were successfully found.

Explain which two missions share a Lagrange-point destination and which is in an Earth orbit, explicitly retaining the wording used by ESA on the overview pages (rather than inferring locations from illustrations). Full credit if the comparison is accurate and uses the source's wording, or if the information was unavailable due to page access issues and the agent clearly states this. Partial credit if the comparison is accurate but wording is inferred or not strictly from the ESA text.

items.criterion: Target population and scientific purpose contrast
items.description: Contrast the target populations and scientific purposes of the three missions so they are distinct and not described as interchangeable planet-search telescopes. Full credit for providing a clear comparative summary distinguishing their scientific goals and targets, or if page unavailability prevented this and the agent explicitly states so.

Provide the URLs for the three ESA mission overview pages used to gather the information. Full credit if all three valid ESA overview URLs are cited, or if the agent provides the URLs attempted but notes they were inaccessible. Partial credit if only one or two URLs are provided when they were available.
